title: EIP-8437: eth/75 - Proof Wrapper Propagation
description: Adds announcement and retrieval of EIP-8288 proof wrappers to eth/75
author: Marc Harvey-Hill (@Marchhill), Daniil Ankushin (@AnkushinDaniil), Manuel Arto (@manusw7), Csaba Kiraly (@cskiraly)
bodyPreview: ## Abstract This EIP defines `eth/75`, a version of the [`eth` wire protocol](https://github.com/ethereum/devp2p/blob/2c19a28b25c29487773ad6b07243e290fa8d65ec/caps/eth.md) that propagates [EIP-8288](./eip-8288.md) proof wrappers ("wrappers" below). Peers announce wrapper modes, lengths and hashes, with the metadata of mode 0 wrappers' transactions, then retrieve wrappers, or the metadata of their transactions, by hash. ## Motivation EIP-8288 separates signatures and proofs from transaction envelopes and permits aggregation across transactions. Existing transaction propagation does not identify this shared proof material, so peers need a way to discover and retrieve it. ## Specification The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in [RFC 2119](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2119) and [RFC 8174](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8174). `eth/75` extends `eth/74`, which extends `eth/73` ([EIP-8408](./eip-8408.md)) with block-level dependency proof retrieval (message IDs 0x16 and 0x17). It uses their message semantics except as specified below. Status (`0x00`) is unchanged; the protocol version and new message IDs are provisional. Request IDs follow [EIP-2481](./eip-2481.md). In the Recursive Length Prefix (RLP) encodings below, `P` is a nonnegative integer (zero encodes as the empty byte string), `B` is a byte string, and `B_n` is a byte string of exactly `n` bytes. The *mempool fork* is the fork selected by the chain's configured activation timestamps at the client's current Unix time in seconds, independently of its head block. EIP-8288 is enabled when included in this fork. Clients MAY negotiate `eth/75` before EIP-8288 is enabled. ### Wrapper encoding The canonical wrapper is the [EIP-8288 wrapper](./eip-8288.md#mempool-wrapper-object) encoded as the RLP list `[transactions, mode, content]`, with: - `transactions`: a nonempty list of complete pooled transaction encodings as byte strings, in strictly ascending consensus transaction-hash order. Blob data is elided as specified under [Blob-carrying dependency transactions](#blob-carrying-dependency-transactions). - `content`: `[deps, proofs]` for mode `0`, or `[deps, recursive_stark]` for mode `1`. - `deps`: a nonempty, strictly byte-lexicographically ordered list of 96-byte dependency encodings as defined by EIP-8288. - `proofs`: one witness byte string per dependency, in dependency order; `recursive_stark`: one nonempty proof byte string. This transport defines `MAX_WRAPPER_BYTES = 2**21` (2 MiB) for the complete canonical RLP encoding; EIP-8288's applicable dependency limits and enabled schemes apply in addition. Hash references are transport-only: clients MUST reconstruct the complete wrapper before applying this bound or computing its hash. ### New messages Messages use canonical RLP with the structures below and no extra fields or trailing bytes. Before EIP-8288 is enabled, clients MUST NOT send wrapper messages and MUST ignore received ones without penalties; underlying transport size limits still apply. #### NewProofWrapperHashes (0x18) `[[mode₀: P, length₀: P, hash₀: B_32, deps-hash₀: B_32, txs-hash₀: B_32, txs-meta₀], ...]` Announce 1–64 held wrappers in strictly ascending hash order: mode is `0` or `1`, length is 1–`MAX_WRAPPER_BYTES`, and hash is Keccak-256 of the complete canonical RLP wrapper, including pooled transaction encodings. Peers SHOULD announce newly validated wrappers to every connected `eth/75` peer and, on connection, up to 64 offered wrappers covering at least one pending transaction, most recent first. Clients MUST ignore announcements of unsupported modes without penalties after checking the message's encoding, count, length and ordering. `deps-hash` is Keccak-256 of the concatenated 96-byte entries in the canonical `deps` list; `txs-hash` is Keccak-256 of the concatenated, ascending consensus transaction hashes. Requesters MAY skip a fetch when both match a held wrapper validated under the current rules. Hints alone establish no coverage or validity; matching only `deps-hash` does not identify the transactions. `txs-meta` lists every transaction of a mode 0 wrapper holding at most 17 transactions. This inline-metadata threshold is fixed for `eth/75`, independently of EIP-8288's validity limits. For other wrappers it is the empty list. Metadata follows wrapper transaction order: `[txtypes: B, [txsize₀: P, ...], [txhash₀: B_32, ...], [txsource₀: B_20, ...], [txnonce₀: P, ...], [txfees₀: [P, ...], ...], [txgas₀: P, ...]]` - `txtypes`: the concatenated [EIP-2718](./eip-2718.md) transaction-type bytes. - `txsize`: the length of the pooled transaction encoding in the complete wrapper. - `txhash`: the consensus transaction hash; the listed hashes concatenate to the preimage of `txs-hash`. - `txsource`: the frame transaction's explicit `sender` field, not a recovered signer. - `txnonce`: its `nonce` field, or `nonce_seq` when [EIP-8250](./eip-8250.md) applies. - `txfees`: a copy of its [EIP-8141](./eip-8141.md) `fees` list. - `txgas`: the sum of its frames' execution and state gas limits. On the wire, nonce and gas are unsigned 64-bit integers, and each fee is an unsigned 256-bit integer; the fee-list length is not fixed. These encoding bounds do not establish transaction validity. Requesters MAY use metadata to choose and order fetches; it establishes no coverage or validity. Metadata omits nonce keys. Receivers MUST NOT compare a frame transaction's `txnonce` with `state[txsource].nonce` to discard an announcement as stale or infer a nonce gap, and MUST use the transaction hash, not `<txsource, txnonce>`, as its identity. Under the same verification rules, peers SHOULD suppress hashes already exchanged on the connection and wrappers whose transactions are covered by held, validated wrappers exchanged with or announced by the recipient, unless they reduce proof
